tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): S3/S4 — startup-failure classification confirmed, process-group cleanup

S3: verified against current source (already fixed by the earlier H1
commit this session): a CRLF-terminated shebang (a hook edited on
Windows, or checked out with core.autocrlf) now reports "the hook
could not be executed at all" rather than the silent (false, nil) the
review reported against an earlier commit. Added a direct regression
test pinning this exact case, since only the mechanism (not this
specific fixture) had been covered before.

S4: confirmed and fixed. A hook that backgrounds a child (`cmd &`,
nohup) has its direct child (the shell) exit quickly and normally —
cmd.Cancel only fires on a context timeout, which never happens in
that case, so the backgrounded grandchild survived past both
hookInvocationObserved returning and the sandbox's own temp-dir
cleanup, running in a directory that had just been deleted. Fixed with
two GOOS-gated files (procgroup_unix.go, procgroup_windows.go — the
Windows side is inert stubs, since sandboxGOOS already refuses before
any command is constructed there): cmd gets its own process group, and
the whole group is SIGKILLed unconditionally right after Run() returns
— not only via Cancel on timeout, which is necessary for the runaway-
loop case but cannot reach an already-orphaned grandchild.

Nit fixed while in this code: os.RemoveAll's error on the sandbox
cleanup was silently discarded, so a hook leaving behind a 0o000
subdirectory leaked the temp dir with no signal. removeSandbox retries
once after forcing every entry's permissions open — filepath.Walk
passes a directory's own readdir failure to walkFn AS that path's
error rather than after, so the chmod has to run unconditionally, not
only when walkErr is nil.

Added a protective comment on cmd.Stdout/Stderr staying nil (S4): it
routes them to /dev/null rather than a pipe, avoiding the classic
os/exec deadlock where a backgrounded child holds a pipe's write end
open past its parent's exit and Wait blocks forever.

Regression tests: a backgrounded subshell and a nohup'd daemon, both
falsified against pre-fix source (2.5s sleep survives cleanup without
the fix, does not survive with it); a locked 0o000 subdirectory for
removeSandbox. `make check` green with race. `GOOS=windows
GOARCH=amd64 go build ./... && go vet ./internal/doctor/...` both exit
0.
EOF
)"
